title: Kähler differentials extend by scalars across a separable algebraic field extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq F\subseteq K$ be fields [def-pc-field-extension] and suppose that $K/F$ is finite ($\dim_F K<\infty$) and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. For the modules of Kähler differentials and universal derivations [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], the canonical $K$-linear map $K\otimes_F\Omega_{F/k}\to\Omega_{K/k}$, $a\otimes\mathrm df\mapsto a\,\mathrm d f$ for $a\in K$ and $f\in F$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031W (lemma-derivative-zero-pth-power), lines 44192-44202: the assertion that Omega_{K/k} is free on dx_i for finite separable K/k(x_i), with the computation omitted; Lemma Tag 090W (lemma-characterize-separable-algebraic-field-extensions), lines 44137-44160, identifies finite separable field extensions as formally étale

A finite separable field extension does not add Kähler differentials: base change of differentials along a separable algebraic extension is an isomorphism
